title: Schema evolution: soft-fallbacks for deprecated fields in streamed tool/function calls
creator: Lina Park
description:
Problem: As customers adopt streaming structured responses and progressive tool/function calling, we need a robust, production-safe approach for schema evolution so that newer model agents can add or deprecate fields without breaking downstream parsers or tools. This ticket defines acceptance criteria and test scenarios for a 'soft-fallback' behavior: when a streamed frame includes a deprecated field or a field from a newer schema version, downstream tooling should be able to continue processing where possible, fall back to compatible behavior, surface clear telemetry, and only escalate to fatal errors when the inconsistency violates required contract guarantees.

Scope: Define version negotiation rules, fallback mapping rules, streaming frame indicators (meta headers), observable error modes, idempotency and resume semantics for tool calls across partial streams, and QA scenarios. Excludes: full-format migration tooling and automatic client-side adapters (these will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Schema version handshake: Every streaming session MUST include a top-level 'schema_version' integer in the first metadata frame. If absent, treat as version 1 for backward compatibility.
Deprecation marker: Fields that are deprecated MUST be emitted with an optional 'deprecated_reason' attribute in the same frame; emitter MAY include 'replacement_field' hint.

Soft-fallback behavior: If consumer sees a field it does not recognize but the schema version is greater than the consumer's supported_version, consumer MUST: 1) record telemetry and the unknown-field name, 2) attempt to parse the rest of the frame ignoring unknown fields, and 3) map to a fallback path if a 'replacement_field' hint is available.

Fatal vs recoverable errors: Missing required top-level envelope properties (conversation_id, frame_id, schema_version) are FATAL and must abort the stream. Unknown nested optional fields are RECOVERABLE and should not abort the stream.

Tool-call resume safety: If a tool-call invocation is interrupted mid-stream, replay/resume must be possible if the stream includes a 'resume_token' with an idempotency pointer; runtime must map resume_token to at-most-once tool invocation semantics where applicable.

Partial-object reconciliation: When a structured object is emitted incrementally across frames, consumer MUST reconstruct in-order by frame_id and validate against consumer-supported schema; missing frames for >5s triggers a partial-recovery heuristic documented in QA steps.

Streaming telemetry: Each stream where soft-fallback behavior is exercised MUST emit a telemetry event containing: schema_version_seen, unknown_field_list, deprecated_field_list, fallback_applied(boolean), and resulting_status(success|partial|error).

Backward compatibility: A consumer supporting up to version N MUST accept streams up to N+1 using soft-fallbacks; streams >N+1 require an explicit compatibility-mode header or are rejected with a clear error code and message.
Operator controls: Console rollout must provide a toggle per-customer to enforce strict schema validation (fatal on unknown fields) vs permissive soft-fallback mode for at least 30-day windows.

E2E tests: Automated tests covering schema bump, deprecated-field presence, unknown nested arrays, resume after interrupt with resume_token, and fail-fast on missing envelope fields must pass in CI before merge.
qa_steps: Create a test model agent that streams a 3-frame progressive object: metadata frame (schema_version:2), first object fragment with deprecated field 'old_action', second fragment with replacement 'action_v2', close frame. Verify consumer records deprecated_field_list and maps to 'action_v2' when replacement hint is present.
Run a scenario where metadata frame omits schema_version. Verify server treats as version 1 and records telemetry 'schema_version_missing' and still processes stream.
Simulate unknown top-level optional field 'experimental_hint' on version N+1; verify consumer ignores field, sets fallback_applied=false, and the stream completes successfully.
Interrupt a tool call mid-stream and resume using resume_token. Verify runtime prevents duplicate side-effects for idempotent-marked tool endpoints and emits a 'resume_success' event.
Enable strict validation in Console for a test workspace and replay a stream with unknown fields; confirm stream rejects and an actionable error is surfaced in the client and logs.
Load test: 1k concurrent streams with mixed schema versions, assert no significant p95 latency regression (>10%) when soft-fallback logic is exercised.
Run security scan on emitted metadata to ensure no secret or PII accidental leakage in replacement hints or deprecated_reason fields.
notes: Decision log (2025-02-17): Use integer schema_version rather than semantic strings to minimize parsing complexity in low-level runtime. Lina + Rohit + Maya agreed.
Trade-offs: permissive mode reduces accidental outages for downstream parsers at cost of potentially hiding incompatible changes; operator toggle mitigates risk for enterprise customers.

Related artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STR/Soft+Fallback+for+Streamed+Schemas (internal), Design sketch: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbcExampleDesignLink, GH PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
Telemetry owners: infra-observability; suggested metric names: redwood.stream.schema_unknown_fields, redwood.stream.deprecated_fields_seen, redwood.stream.fallbacks_applied_total.
Estimated effort: 5 points (API surface + runtime parsing + console toggle + e2e tests).
